summary: A Barry County lookout site now best known as the Pine View Tower Trailhead into the Piney Creek Wilderness; no source confirms a tower stands there.

facts.agency: Mark Twain National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

access.note: The Forest Service lists the Pine View Tower Trailhead as open, with three primitive campsites. Its page does not say whether a tower can be climbed.

visit.trail_note: Two paths of about 1.5 miles each run south from the trailhead to Piney Creek, 3.8 miles in total.

evidence.supports: trailhead is a Forest Service site in Mark Twain National Forest
evidence.quote: Mark Twain National Forest | Pine View Tower Trailhead | Forest Service

evidence.supports: Pine View tower is the northern access to the Piney Creek Wilderness
evidence.quote: Pine View tower is the northern access to the Piney Creek Wilderness.
The United States Congress designated it wilderness in 1980.

evidence.supports: three primitive campsites with picnic tables and fire rings
evidence.quote: There are 3 primitive campsites with picnic tables and fire rings.

evidence.supports: two paths of about 1.5 miles each, 3.8 miles in all, to Piney Creek
evidence.quote: two paths of approximately 1.5 miles each, for a total of 3.8 miles, leads south to Piney Creek.

evidence.supports: approach 5.5 miles west of Cape Fair on Highway 76, off Farm Road 2150
evidence.quote: the Pineview (Tower) Trailhead is 5.5 miles west of Cape Fair on Highway 76 off Farm road 2150

evidence.supports: the spot where the original fire tower stood can still be seen, per the Forest Service page for the site
evidence.quote: views of the original fire tower site can still be found

sources.title: Pine View Tower Trailhead

notes_for_editor: Status, height, design and construction date are not in any source I could reach, so the record keeps status unknown. The Central US Lookouts page is a bare county listing with no history. The NHLR and FFLOS caches have no Pineview entry. News-Leader (Nov 2018, Mark Twain fire towers) and Missouri Life returned HTTP 403, WebFetch refused the News-Leader page, and Trailforks returned 403; these are the likeliest places for Pineview's history and should be read by a person or another route. The 1980 wilderness date comes from Wikipedia and should be checked against the Forest Service wilderness record. Forest Service pages describe the trailhead, not who owns the tower, so ownership stays as the record has it. Whether a tower stands on the site now is unverified.
